title: Pass a wafer carrier through an airlock whose two gates are never open at once
instruction: Pass the carrier through the airlock to the stop on the left and shut both gates. The two gates must never be open at the same time, and the carrier must stay on the lane.
context: Semiconductor technicians pass wafer carriers between cleanroom zones through pass-through airlocks. Only one door may ever be open, or dirty air reaches the clean side, so the second door waits until the first is fully shut. Here each gate is in reach of only one arm, so the arms have to take turns.
setup: Station table; distances from the arm bases' line are forward, and left or right from the point midway between the arms. A fixed steel lane on two steel legs, its centre line 22 cm forward, running left to right and falling 10 degrees toward the left: 48 cm long, its surface 4.5 cm above the table at the centre, 6.6 cm wide between two steel side rails 2 cm tall, with a slick plastic surface (friction 0.05). The rails stop for 3.2 cm at each gate. A fixed steel stop 4 cm tall closes its low end, its face 20.7 cm left of centre. Two red ABS gates (each 11 cm wide, 2 cm thick, 11 cm tall, 0.25 kg) stand across the lane, gate A 9.4 cm right of centre and gate B 9.4 cm left of centre, each sliding up and down in two fixed steel channels that reach 8.5 cm above the gate's lower edge; nothing but a hand holds a gate up. Between the gates, a chamber of two fixed steel walls 8.6 cm apart and 14.7 cm long, reaching 13 cm above the table at its roof of 1 cm steel bars with 15 mm gaps. A hollow white plastic wafer carrier (6 x 10 x 4 cm, 0.15 kg), its 10 cm side along the lane, rests on the lane with its nose 2 mm from gate A.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial. A gate is open when its lower edge is more than 1 cm above where it closes, and shut when within 3 mm. 0 if the carrier ever rises more than 1 cm off the lane or moves more than 2 cm from the lane's centre line. Otherwise: 1.0 if the carrier's nose is within 1 cm of the stop, both gates are shut, they were never open at the same time, and carrier and gates are still for 1 second. 0.5 if the carrier's nose is within 1 cm of the stop and both gates are shut, but they were once open at the same time. 0.25 if the carrier is wholly between the gates, both are shut, and they were never open at the same time. 0 otherwise. In a real trial, a side video against 1 cm marks on a card beside each gate shows when each gate is open; a tape measure from the stop checks the carrier.
reset_notes: Shut both gates and rest the carrier on the lane with its nose 2 mm from gate A; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: All parts are rigid. There is no air: the gates are plain plates sliding in channels, without seals or an electrical interlock, and the rule that they are never open together is what is scored. The lane is a low-friction surface, so the carrier slides. Nothing is deformable.
